Q: SSAS & SCD2 - how to deal with IsActive row in Dim A:

SCD2 is working exactly as designed here fact row 101 is supposed to point to the old record because that was the truth at the time of the call. Thats the whole point of type 2.

If you want reports to always show the current gender regardless of when the call hapened, the trick is to join through the business key instead of the surrogate key. So your fact table still references SK=2 (old Jo), but in your query you go from that old dimension row, grab the AltKey (16), and then find the row where AltKey=16 and IsActive=1, wich gives you the current details. Two joins to the same dimension table basically — one to follow the fact's SK, another to get the current active row via the shared AltKey.

This way you dont break your SCD2 model, you keep the historical truth available when you need it, and you can also report on current atributes whenever thats what the business wants. Best of both worlds.

Q: How can I merge two dataframes based on range of dates? A:

I have tested this solution out and it should work for you. Creating a new column which represents the end of your range for df1 will allow you to use a function to iterate over each row and then check whether or not your id matches.

Creating the new column:

df1['end'] = df1['a'] + pd.Timedelta(hours=3)

Iterating over each row:

def get_matching_id(row):
  for _, r in df1.iterrows():
    if r['a'] <= row['a'] <= r['end']:
      return r['id']
  return pd.NA

Apply the function:

df2['id'] = df2.apply(get_matching_id, axis=1)

This should assign your ids to each row in df2 if it falls within the range we created. This is probably not super performant for large scale pandas, and the fact that we're doing candlesticks analysis here makes me think that maybe volume is an issue. There's very similar solutions to be had if we need to migrate to Spark dataframes.

Q: ggplot2::ggsave will not export custom fonts A:

This answer gives full credit to @Abigail. First, I added showtext_auto() right before the plot, which made ggsave work correctly, but then the issue was there was extra spacing between the lines of text.

I found a discussion of this issue on the showtext github here. The issue was the the ggsave and showtext dpi defaults were different (300 and 96, respectively). So adding showtext_opts(dpi = 300) before the plot also solved that problem.

Final code, with solution, below:

library(ggplot2)

showtext::showtext_auto()
showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

a <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg)) + geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Fuel Efficiency of 32 Cars") +
  xlab("Weight (x1000 lb)") + ylab("Miles per Gallon") +
  theme(text=element_text(size=16,  family="Larsseit-BoldItalic"))

a

ggsave(filename = "~/Desktop/test_plot.png", 
       plot=a, 
       width= 5.64*2, 
       height=3.58*2, 
       dpi=300)

Q: How should Dockerfiles and Docker Compose configurations be managed for development and production environments in Docker? A:

In your development setup, don't use Docker at all, except maybe for some supporting programs like a database or a memory cache. Use your host OS's package manager to install a language runtime, or use a dedicated version-manager tool; see for example RVM equivalent for PHP?

With this setup, you can have a single (production-oriented) image and a single Compose setup, and you can use the standard file names Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml for them.

There are some common setups that use Docker "to not need to install software on the host". But of course you are installing the language runtime by downloading its Docker image, and now you need to do some awkward steps whenever you'd need to use the tooling in the container. By design, the host system can't see programs in the container filesystem, and the container can't see the source code you're developing on the host. This isn't a good match for frequently needing to run things like unit tests or for live debugging. (See other [docker] questions for ongoing problems with live reloading on file changes, or connecting your IDE's debugger to a language runtime isolated in a container.)

Q: How to do left join without duplicates rows sql A:

Use distinct


SELECT distinct
      d.lead_id,
      d.owner,
      d.status,
      a."activity" as "activity type"
FROM  "Deals Table" d
LEFT JOIN "Activity Table" a ON d."lead_id"  = a."lead_id"  ;
